Subject: Pilot request: nonprofit pricing & baseline hosted API rates

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking a look — OpenHands runs literacy programs in five states and we're putting together a small ML pilot to add automated reading-comprehension feedback into our tutor app. Before we schedule a demo we'd like to confirm whether Redwood offers nonprofit/startup pilot pricing and what the hosted API baseline rates look like for a 3-month pilot.

High-level pilot details:
- Duration: 3 months (Sept–Nov provisional)
- Expected usage: ~1.5M tokens/month average, spikes up to ~3M tokens in peak weeks
- Models: short-form chat for student prompts + embeddings for search/reranking

Specific questions:
1) Are you able to offer a nonprofit pilot discount or credits for a registered 501(c)(3)?
2) What baseline hosted API rates should we budget for after pilot credits expire?
3) Any standard paperwork or evidence you need (proof of nonprofit, PO, W9)?

I attached a short mission brief and a one-page program budget for context. Happy to jump on a quick call if that's easier.

Best,
Nina Bowers

Hi Nina — great to meet you (virtually), and thanks for the context — this is exactly the sort of program we like to support. Short answers up front, followed by details and next steps.

Yes — eligibility and what we can offer:
- Nonprofit pilot: we can provision a 3-month pilot with a subsidized rate (pilot credit + discounted per-unit pricing) for registered 501(c)(3) organizations.
- Baseline hosted API pricing: for standard generator/chat models our public baseline is $2.50 per 1k tokens; embeddings are priced separately at $1.00 per 1k embedding units.
- Pilot offer we typically propose: up to 100k free tokens per month + a reduced rate of $0.50 per 1k tokens for the first 3 months on usage beyond the free allocation (cap negotiable based on expected volume).

Conditions and operational items:
- We require proof of nonprofit status (IRS determination letter or national equivalent) and a contact for billing/procurement.
- Pilot will be provisioned on our hosted stack under a short MOU (no enterprise Dedicated commitment). If you require private deployment or reserved capacity, pricing moves to a separate Dedicated plan.
- Standard billing terms after pilot: Net 30, invoices monthly.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Send proof of nonprofit and procurement contact (procurement@openhands.org is fine).
2) I can loop in Legal to prepare a short pilot MOU / pilot SOW and a DocuSign link.
3) Schedule a 30-minute kickoff + a short technical onboarding with Monica (CC'd) to scope token patterns and ingestion.

I've CC'd Marissa (Sales Ops) to prepare a one-page commercial summary and Monica (CS) to lead onboarding. If that sounds good I'll get a draft MOU to you by Monday.

Thanks — Olga

Hi Nina / team — Rafael from Legal here. Olga looped me in to finalise the pilot MOU and clarify commercial terms.

Short answers to procurement questions and what you'll see in the draft MOU:
- Credits vs invoice: pilot subsidy will be implemented as an account-level credit applied to monthly invoices. The invoice will show the gross usage, the pilot credit line, and the net due.
- Overage pricing: for the first 3 months we will honor the negotiated pilot rate ($0.50 / 1k) up to the agreed monthly cap. Any usage beyond the cap will be billed at baseline rate ($2.50 / 1k) unless you agree to an expanded cap in writing.
- Billing terms: Net 30. We can accept a PO number on invoices.
- Data & compliance: hosted pilot will include standard Pine (sic) audit logs for usage; retention and audit access details are in the MOU appendix. If you require longer retention or SOC2 addendums we can add those as an appendix (may affect pricing).

I've attached a short pilot-MOA-draft.pdf (pilot MOU + SOW). Next steps from our side:
1) Nina: confirm preferred monthly cap (suggested starting point: 250k tokens/month beyond free allocation).
2) OpenHands procurement: confirm billing contact and whether PO numbers will be used.
3) If agreed, we'll send the DocuSign and schedule the onboarding.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
